I wonder what kind of impact that would have on the backend to do that sort of math and not have it cached. By having it the same for everyone you can calculate a temporary score based on ups, downs, time, and any modifying factor. This score can be universal for the sake of sorting for every user and recalculated every second with very low impact. If you change the modifying factor on a per user basis the whole process will have to be done per page query which is far more often that once a second.

There's a balancing here possible between computation and bandwidth. If computation becomes the bottleneck or cost cap then the server could instead of sorting the data itself instead just keep your sort criteria and send that over to you along with a large blob of cached data. The sort itself would be carried out locally before rendering a segment of that blob. Practically free computation wise, but heavy bandwidth wise. As bandwidth becomes the cost cap then you can begin going the other direction and doing some filtering server side to minimize the blob size.
